name: Manuel Noriega
summary: Noriega ruled Panama through the Panama Defense Forces after taking command in 1983, without holding the presidency. He relied on military power, the Dignity Battalions and control of the press, annulled the May 1989 election, and framed his confrontation with the United States in nationalist terms. His own stated ideology is not recorded beyond these rhetorical and practical positions.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: A pilot testified that Noriega authorized weapons flights to Sandinista and Salvadoran guerrillas, and an official that he gave the Contras training bases; the testimony is contested.

consent-of-governed.rationale: He annulled the 1989 election and ruled by military force; the Inter-American Commission found his regime devoid of constitutional legitimacy.

defeat-communism.rationale: His record points both ways: bases and training for the anti-Sandinista Contras, but also authorized arms flights to leftist guerrillas.

democracy-best.rationale: He annulled the May 1989 election the opposition had apparently won and installed an unelected provisional government, overriding the voters.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: No known position: annulling one election does not settle whether fair elections are enough to make a government democratic.

dominated-front.rationale: No known position: his call was for a common front within Panama, not for countries dominated by the West to unite.

independent-unions.rationale: His regime effectively controlled almost all labor organizations, arrested union officials and closed a union's offices, exempting only regime-controlled bodies from its war laws.

military-guardian-role.rationale: No known position: his military rule does not settle whether armed forces should guard the constitutional order.

nation-first.rationale: No known position: his sovereignty rhetoric fits either answer on putting national interest ahead of global cooperation.

party-controls-media.rationale: His regime closed all opposition media in 1988, took over two television stations and tightened control of radio in 1989.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: His regime held mass trials without due process, ignored habeas corpus writs and detained people without charge, and ruled by decree.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: In October 1989 his regime abolished the right to strike and abolished public employee associations by decree.

separated-powers.rationale: Human Rights Watch reports the executive and judiciary were subordinated to the PDF, and the State Department that courts were PDF-controlled and ignored habeas corpus.

strong-leader.rationale: He ruled through the Panama Defense Forces, placed the executive and judiciary under military control and governed by decree after annulling the 1989 election.

suppress-opposition.rationale: His forces beat and jailed opposition leaders, shut the opposition press, annulled the 1989 election and used Dignity Battalions against opposition candidates and demonstrators.

notes: Later pass 2026-11-23. Replaced the Wikipedia citations with the reports it relies on (US State Department 1989 human-rights report, Human Rights Watch, the federal court opinion, AP report of the 1988 Senate testimony, Britannica). Searched the themes government, liberty, world, means and society; economy, culture, ecology and technology have no record. His own memoir and speeches are in notFound; most statements are null. Four earlier answers resting on words or on a record that does not settle the statement were nulled. The 15 December 1989 'state of war' was declared by the National Assembly at his instigation, and he named himself no ideology.
